answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with identity-bound stake: each participant locks a bond mirrored on the ledger, so weight follows locked value, not name count. A checkpoint, a knoll above the tundra of easy signups, fixes each agent's history so a fresh mirror cannot impersonate an older one. Splitting one bond among fake agents gains nothing, since the mirror reveals duplicate stakes and each checkpoint caps one identity per bond. To sway a vote an attacker must lock real value proportional to influence sought; on that tundra the costly part is the stake, not the signup.
